title: Quantum Characteristic Classes
html:
Definition. Quantum Characteristic Classes

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe. Let \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} be its recursive brane tower. Each transition A_n \hookrightarrow A_{n+1} in \mathbf{C} defines a central extension of gerbes on the underlying site. The Frobenius–Hopf object A_n is an object in a gerbe \mathfrak{G}_n banded by the sheaf of units \mathcal{B}. The jet prolongation produces a central extension:

  1  \longrightarrow  \mathcal{B}
   \longrightarrow  \mathfrak{G}_{n+1}
   \longrightarrow  \mathfrak{G}_n
   \longrightarrow  1.

The quantum characteristic classes are the cohomology classes

  \kappa_n  \in  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B})

that obstruct the lifting of objects from \mathfrak{G}_n to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1}. By the Quantum lifting condition, the condition \kappa_n = 0 is necessary and sufficient for the lift to exist.
